editorial:
Imagine you are visiting a quiet little town in California that is celebrating its 100th birthday. Everything seems normal until weird stuff starts happening. You will meet a mix of locals, like a radio DJ and a priest, who all start noticing that something is very wrong. A thick, glowing fog rolls into town, and inside that mist are the ghosts of dead sailors coming back for revenge. The whole movie feels like a creepy campfire story, with a slow build-up that makes you feel like something bad is just around the corner. It is not about jump scares; it is about the mood and the mystery.

What really works here is how the tension grows as the fog moves closer. The acting is solid, and the music keeps you on edge the whole time. While it moves a bit slowly at the start, the payoff is great. If you like old-school horror that relies on atmosphere rather than gore, you will love this.
endingExplained: You find out that the town founders betrayed a group of sailors long ago to steal their gold. Now, those dead sailors have returned as ghosts in the fog to kill everyone. In the end, the survivors fight back and manage to stop the ghosts. The movie wraps up with the town safe, but it leaves you knowing that the greed of the past is what caused the nightmare in the first place.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves atmospheric ghost stories and 80s horror.
